data.hypothesis: Using 16-pixel tiles with an explicit OpenMP SIMD length of 16 may reduce per-pixel tile and loop overhead compared with the valid 8-lane parent, if the frozen compiler maps this portable SIMD request efficiently. The test preserves each lane's recurrence, active-lane logic, tail handling, and original float coordinate expressions; no ISA-specific instruction or scheduling change is assumed.
data.notes: The catalog has one distinct T2 program and no repeated program. The measured parent (4bc6af7262ba4416) was valid at mean 0.303312 s, compared with baseline-e1 at 0.563422 s; these results do not establish performance on shifted bounds. This candidate has not been built or measured here. The controller should verify frozen-configuration build/run availability and exact counts for target, smaller, and shifted-bound cases. The run path ignores threads, so any result under the four-core budget remains a one-thread SIMD result, not a four-core result. No ISA-specific variant is proposed.
transformations: Expanded the adjacent-pixel tile and lane-state arrays from 8 to 16 lanes.
Requested OpenMP SIMD length 16 on lane initialization, recurrence, and valid-lane output loops; retained active-lane reduction and early termination.
Preserved x0 + pixel * dx and y0 + j * dy coordinate calculations, recurrence order, tail masking, output layout, and thread-ignoring run path.
